data.title: iOS 27 dropped today: The prep steps nobody tells you about
data.description:
Apple’s iOS 27 is rolling out today, Sept. 14, and if you have not prepared your iPhone yet, there are a few things worth doing before you hit that install button.


The update supports iPhone 11 and newer, covering the same device range as iOS 26. While this release is less of a visual overhaul than last year’s Liquid Glass redesign, it brings meaningful performance improvements, a revamped Siri and enough under-the-hood changes to make a proper preparation worthwhile before you dive in.


Clear space and charge your battery first

The update process requires temporary file storage on top of the download itself, so aim for at least 18 to 25 gigabytes of free space before you begin. If your storage is running close to the limit, clearing out unused apps, old photos and cached data can get you there.

Battery level matters too. A charge of at least 50% should technically be enough to complete the update, but running the process while plugged in is the safer choice. Keep Wi-Fi connected throughout, as the update will not download on cellular by default.


Back up before you do anything else

This is the step that tends to get skipped. Major updates can occasionally cause data loss or unexpected issues, and recovering from a failed update without a backup is painful.

Go to Settings, tap your Apple Account, select iCloud, then iCloud Backup and tap Back Up Now. If you prefer a local backup, connect your phone to a Mac or Windows computer and run a backup through Finder or iTunes. Either way, have your Apple ID credentials nearby in case something prompts you to verify your account during or after the installation.

If you are still running an earlier version, it is also worth checking whether you have updated to iOS 26.6. Apple built an indexing update into that release specifically to make the transition to iOS 27’s new Siri framework smoother.

Choose how you want to update

You have two options. To let your phone update on its own, go to Settings, then General, then Software Update, then Automatic Updates and enable Automatically Install. Your phone will update overnight while it is charging and connected to Wi-Fi. To install it yourself the moment it is available, stay on the Software Update page and tap when the prompt appears.

What is actually new in iOS 27

Speed is the headline. Apple says apps launch up to 30% faster, photos appear in your library up to 70% faster after you take them, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% faster. Smaller touches include faster emoji keyboard loading and quicker switching between lock screen setups.

Liquid Glass returns from iOS 26 but with a new customization slider in Settings, letting you control how much of the glass effect appears across the interface. Contrast and depth on app icons have also been improved.

The biggest functional addition is the new Siri, rebuilt to compete more directly with tools like Gemini and ChatGPT. iOS 27 also introduces a smarter alarm system that learns your daily patterns and adjusts accordingly, along with new child safety features and a more readable overall design.

data.title: Why is Elon Musk betting big on AI and robots?
data.description:
Elon Musk has put a striking timeline on his vision for an economy powered by artificial intelligence and robots. The Tesla chief has suggested that AI and machines could more than double the size of the global economy in less than a decade.


The prediction sounds enormous. The math behind it is even more revealing.


The global economy is expected to produce roughly $126 trillion in 2026, according to International Monetary Fund projections. Doubling that figure would mean reaching about $252 trillion in annual economic output by 2036.

To double an economy in 10 years, annual growth would need to average about 7.2% every year. If the timeline is shortened to nine years, the required pace rises to roughly 8%. Over eight years, it would be about 9% annually.


That is considerably faster than the world’s current growth rate.

The IMF projects global growth of about 3% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027. At a steady 3% pace, the global economy would take roughly 23 years to double.

Musk’s projection therefore requires the world economy to accelerate dramatically and maintain that pace for years.

There is an important distinction, however. Musk has not clearly specified whether his prediction refers to real economic output or nominal dollar growth. Nominal figures include inflation and currency effects, meaning a larger dollar value does not necessarily represent the production of twice as many goods and services.

Musk’s bigger vision for AI and robots

Musk has been making increasingly ambitious predictions about the economic impact of AI and robotics.

During a virtual appearance at the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, N.C., on Sept. 1, he discussed the possibility that AI could eventually add between $20 trillion and $30 trillion to annual global economic output.

He has also predicted that at least 1 billion robots could be operating within a decade. His vision assumes those machines would eventually produce significantly more economic output than human workers.

That projection places enormous importance on manufacturing capacity, technology development and electricity supplies.

Musk has warned that the rapid expansion of AI computing could create major demands for electricity. He has pointed to a potential power shortage of about 15 gigawatts in 2027 as data centers and AI infrastructure expand.

The robot industry is growing, but its current scale remains far below Musk’s long-term vision.

China, one of the leading markets for humanoid robots, is expected to ship about 50,000 units in 2026. That forecast was raised substantially from an earlier estimate of 14,000 units.

By 2030, annual Chinese humanoid shipments are projected to reach about 446,000 units.

Those numbers represent rapid growth, but they also illustrate how far the industry would have to expand to reach a global fleet of 1 billion machines.

The impact could reach workers and investors

The economic transformation Musk describes would have major consequences for employees, businesses and investors.

Companies adopting AI and robotics could potentially produce more goods and services with fewer workers. That could increase productivity and corporate profits, while also changing which skills employers value.

The transition is already influencing employment decisions. Artificial intelligence was cited as the reason for more than 116,000 announced U.S. job cuts through August, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas.

That figure does not mean robots are directly replacing all of those workers. Instead, it demonstrates that expectations surrounding AI are already affecting corporate decisions before the technology reaches Musk’s proposed scale.

Tesla investors have another reason to watch the robotics race closely. Optimus, the company’s humanoid robot project, is part of Musk’s broader strategy for the company and features prominently in discussions surrounding his compensation and Tesla’s future growth.

For investors, however, the most important numbers may not be Musk’s headline projections.

Robot production, electricity availability and productivity gains will determine whether the world can approach the extraordinary growth rates required by his forecast.

If those figures accelerate dramatically, the global economy could look very different by the middle of the next decade. If they fail to keep pace, the more familiar 3% growth environment could remain the better guide.

Musk has supplied a bold vision for the robot economy. The difficult part will be turning the vision into enough machines, power and productivity to make the math work.

data.title: Nintendo’s 30% sale has a controversial backstory
data.description:
Nintendo is offering one of its biggest sales in years, and the backstory behind the discount is nearly as interesting as the deals themselves.


The company announced a Customer Appreciation Sale today giving American customers 30% off dozens of Nintendo Switch digital games and bundles, plus discounts on select physical games, downloadable content, accessories, amiibo and apparel. The sale runs September 13 through September 26 across the Nintendo eShop, Nintendo Store and participating retailers.


The reason for the out-of-season promotion, as Nintendo put it, is a thank-you to players for their continued support, made possible in part by tariff-related refunds. That framing has landed with decidedly mixed reactions from the gaming community.

The messy history behind the sale

The backstory starts with the sweeping tariffs President Donald Trump imposed on imports from more than 180 countries. Nintendo, along with other gaming giants, raised its prices in response, hiking Switch console prices by $30 to $50 and bumping accessory costs by $5 to $10.


When the Supreme Court later ruled those tariffs unlawful, the government began refunding import duties to companies that had paid them. Nintendo received approximately $300 million in tariff refunds.

Rather than passing those savings to the customers who had absorbed the higher prices, Nintendo initially said buyers were not entitled to refunds because they had received exactly what they bargained and paid for at prices both parties agreed to. A class-action lawsuit from customers seeking those refunds is still pending in court.

Prices, notably, have still not returned to pre-tariff levels.

Nintendo of America announces Customer Appreciation Sale
by
u/Skullghost in
gaming

What the sale actually offers

The 30% discount applies to a broad selection of Switch titles and other company gaming products across digital and physical retail. The company has not yet published the complete list of included games and products, but buyers can check the Nintendo eShop and Nintendo Store starting September 13 for the full catalog.

Frequently asked questions

Will I get money back for the higher prices I paid during the tariff period? No. The company has maintained in ongoing litigation that customers who purchased at tariff-era prices received exactly what they paid for and are not owed refunds. The 30% sale is a promotional discount on future purchases, not compensation for past ones.

Can I use the sale discount in-store at retailers like Best Buy or Target? It says participating retail locations are included, though available products and offers may vary by retailer and sales channel. Check with your specific store before heading in.

Do prices go back to normal after the sale ends? They have not indicated any plans to return prices to pre-tariff levels after the sale concludes on September 26. The promotion is a temporary discount, not a permanent price correction.

data.title: Samsung’s savage jab at Apple’s new foldable phone goes viral
data.description:
Samsung wasted no time turning Apple’s biggest announcement of the year into a punchline. Within hours of Apple unveiling its first foldable phone, Samsung’s social media team fired off a string of jokes aimed squarely at its longtime rival, and the internet ran with it. What started as a single cheeky post has since snowballed into a full rollout of digs, screenshots and callbacks that fans are calling one of the sharpest brand rivalries in recent memory.


Let us know when you’re done reheating our leftovers 😉

— Samsung Mobile US (@SamsungMobileUS) September 9, 2026

Samsung’s opening shot went viral fast

The moment Apple’s foldable device went live, Samsung posted a simple line poking fun at how long it took its rival to catch up to a form factor Samsung has sold for years. The post read like a friendly jab on the surface, but the timing made it impossible to miss the target. Within minutes, the reply count climbed into the thousands, and screenshots of the exchange spread across timelines far beyond the tech crowd that usually follows product launches.


Samsung didn’t stop there. Over the following hours, the account kept posting variations on the same theme, comparing the wait for Apple’s foldable to stale leftovers, a groundhog repeating the same day and a homework assignment turned in years late. Each post leaned on a specific detail from Apple’s own marketing, twisting the language just enough to land as a wink rather than a direct insult. That approach has become something of a signature for Samsung’s social team, which has built a reputation for jumping on rival announcements the moment they happen.

Samsung takes shots at Apple on X after Apple announced its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo.

“Let us know when you’re done reheating our leftovers” pic.twitter.com/TjeJaNMCyf

— Daily Loud (@DailyLoud) September 10, 2026

Why the timing landed so well

Part of what made this round of jokes hit differently is how long Samsung has been selling foldable phones compared with Apple. Years of head start gave Samsung’s marketing team a deep well of material to pull from, and the brand leaned into that gap rather than shying away from it. Fans quickly picked up on the pattern and began replying with their own versions of the joke, turning the exchange into a running bit that extended well past the original post.


Apple, for its part, has stayed silent on the exchange, which is fairly typical for a company that rarely engages directly with competitor jabs on social media. That silence hasn’t slowed the momentum of the joke online, if anything, it has given fans more room to keep the bit alive without any pushback from the other side.

A rivalry that keeps finding new material

This isn’t the first time a major phone launch has turned into an online sparring match between the two brands, and it likely won’t be the last. Product launches in this industry tend to draw an audience that is already primed to compare specs, pricing and design choices the moment new hardware goes public, which makes the window for a viral response extremely short. Samsung’s team has clearly built its process around moving fast in that window rather than waiting to see how the news cycle plays out.

For everyday users, the exchange is mostly entertainment rather than a meaningful signal about either company’s actual product strategy. Still, moments like this tend to shape public perception in ways that outlast the joke itself, reinforcing an image of Samsung as the scrappier, faster-moving rival even when the two companies are, in practice, competing for the exact same customers. Whether that goodwill translates into actual sales remains an open question, but for one afternoon, Samsung clearly won the internet.

The bigger picture behind the banter

Marketing analysts who track how brands behave online have pointed out that Samsung’s approach works because it never crosses into outright mockery. Every post stays close enough to a real product detail that it reads as commentary rather than an attack, which keeps the tone light even as the jokes pile up. That balance is part of why fans have kept the momentum going instead of dismissing it as a company simply being petty toward a competitor.

The brand has leaned into this style of rapid response for several product cycles now, and the pattern has become something audiences actively look forward to whenever a major Apple event rolls around. Whether this particular exchange fades within a day or lingers as one of the more memorable moments of the year, it has already accomplished what Samsung’s marketing team clearly set out to do, keeping its own name squarely in the conversation during a week that was supposed to belong entirely to Apple.

data.title: Foldable iPhone Duo is here, and Samsung is not letting it slide
data.description:
Apple unveiled its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, at Today’s fall event in Cupertino, marking the biggest redesign to the iPhone lineup in years. The device opens into a 7.6 inch inner display, the largest screen ever put on an iPhone, and closes down to a 5.4 inch outer display for one handed use. Pricing starts at 1,999 dollars for the 256GB model, climbing up through 512GB, 1TB and 2TB configurations, with pre orders opening October 16 and units shipping October 23. New CEO John Ternus led the keynote, his first as Apple’s chief executive after taking over from Tim Cook at the start of the month.


How does the price compare to Samsung’s foldable

Apple’s pricing lands almost exactly where analysts expected, and notably close to Samsung’s own foldable flagship. The Galaxy Z Fold8 starts around 100 dollars cheaper at retail, which means Apple did not try to dramatically undercut its biggest foldable rival the way some reports predicted earlier this year. Where Apple appears to have an edge is stylus support, since the Duo is expected to work with Apple Pencil while Samsung dropped S Pen compatibility starting with the Z Fold7 in order to shave down thickness and weight.


What is actually new inside the foldable design

Beyond the dual displays, the Duo runs on Apple’s A20 Pro chip paired with a custom vapor chamber and dual battery architecture, aimed at solving the heat and battery life problems that have plagued foldables from every manufacturer. The camera system includes a 48 megapixel main sensor and an ultra wide lens, though notably no dedicated telephoto camera, a gap Samsung’s Z Fold8 shares. Software features lean into the split screen format, letting owners run two full apps side by side, open two windows of the same app for things like comparison shopping, or keep a conversation going with the new Siri AI assistant while working in another app on the second half of the screen.

APPLE FINALLY MADE A FOLDABLE iPHONE OH THIS EATS😭😭😭 #AppleEvent pic.twitter.com/Rtl5h59gV2

— 𝗱𝗮𝗻𝗻𝘆🫧💚 (@beyoncegarden) September 9, 2026

Why is Samsung trolling Apple on launch day

This is where the day got more entertaining than a typical Apple keynote. Samsung’s official U.S. social account posted a string of jabs throughout the event, needling Apple over how long it took to enter the foldable category and mocking the accessory lineup as an afterthought without real substance. Hours before Apple’s presentation even started, Samsung had already released a commercial branded around welcoming Apple to the foldable market, leaning hard into claims that the Z Fold8 is lighter and thinner than anything Apple was about to announce. Samsung’s own research team told reporters that weight remains the single hardest engineering problem in foldable design, a not so subtle shot aimed directly at Apple’s newcomer status in the category.


How big of a business opportunity is a foldable actually

Foldables remain a small slice of the overall smartphone market, expected to make up roughly 2.2% of global units this year according to research firm IDC, rising slowly to around 3.1% by 2030. But because foldables carry a much higher price tag than standard phones, that same sliver of unit sales is expected to generate close to 7% of total smartphone revenue this year, climbing toward 10% by the end of the decade. That math is likely why Apple decided the category was finally worth entering, even as Huawei continues to dominate foldable sales in China and Samsung holds the lead across most of the rest of the world.

What happens next for Apple’s stock and the rest of the lineup

Apple also announced the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, both getting a 100 dollar price increase tied to rising memory costs, along with the Apple Watch Series 12, Watch Ultra 4 and updated AirPods 5. Apple shares dipped modestly in the hours after the event, which analysts note is a fairly normal pattern for iPhone launch days, with the stock historically recovering and posting gains in the 60 days following past reveals. Whether the Duo becomes Apple’s next major growth driver or a niche experiment will likely take those same 60 days, and a lot more real world hands-on time, to sort out.

data.title: 3 GTA 6 reveals stir fresh Trailer 3 frenzy this week
data.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI devotees are once again glued to Rockstar Games’ social media accounts, and this time the calendar is doing the heavy lifting. Take-Two Interactive has set its annual virtual shareholder meeting for Wednesday, Sept. 17, a webcast presentation that arrives just weeks after the studio’s extended look at the game. With the Nov. 19 release date locked in, the community’s attention has shifted to one lingering wish: a third trailer.


Why the hope keeps building comes down to timing and history. Rockstar has a habit of pairing major reveals with corporate moments, and an investor call in front of shareholders feels, to fans, like exactly the kind of stage the studio might use.


On the company’s August call, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick reaffirmed the launch date and described GTA 6 pre-orders as astronomical, language that only sharpened the appetite for something new before Wednesday.

3 events keeping the frenzy alive

Three developments are stacking up in the same short window and feeding the trailer speculation.


The first (1) is the shareholder meeting itself, scheduled for 6 p.m. PT on Sept. 17. Because past calls have delivered fresh details, fans see it as a natural launch point for a story trailer centered on protagonists Jason and Lucia and their main storyline.

The second (2) is GTA 6’s appearance at PlayStation’s Tokyo Game Show booth later in the week, where attendees can pick up a free T-shirt, stickers and exclusive merchandise on the show floor.

The third (3) is Rockstar’s summer marketing push, which has been rolling out steadily and shows no sign of slowing before the game arrives.

A Miami Beach deal draws debate

Part of that marketing effort has already stirred controversy. Miami Beach commissioners voted 4-3 to approve a roughly $3 million branding campaign with Rockstar, timed to the game’s release and running from Oct. 15 to Dec. 31. Anyone picturing the city transformed into the fictional Vice City will be let down, since the plan was pitched as discreet and understated, leaning mostly on the Roman numeral six.

Not everyone on the commission was comfortable with it. Some members worried that tying the city to a franchise built around crime and vice would undercut recent efforts to shed a reputation for spring break chaos.

Others framed the partnership as a friendly nod to the many longtime players who have followed the series for decades. The game is set in a Miami-inspired world, which made the local tie-in a natural, if contentious, fit.

What fans should actually expect

For all the anticipation, nothing about a Trailer 3 has been confirmed. Most of the core information about GTA 6 is already public, and demand is running hot regardless, with pre-orders topping charts on PS5 and Xbox and GTA 6-themed DualSense controllers already being scalped for hundreds of dollars online. Leaks have also pointed to a possible collector’s edition featuring a Vice City-styled box and a disc slot.

Whether Rockstar delivers a full story trailer, a shorter promo or nothing new at all, the studio has kept its plans close. Wednesday’s meeting will show whether the wait for another look ends this week or stretches closer to the November launch.

data.title: iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders open with 5 exciting new upgrades
data.description:
Apple is preparing to launch its newest iPhone lineup, with pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max opening Saturday at 5 a.m. Pacific time on apple.com and through the Apple Store app.


The new devices arrive alongside an expanded lineup that includes the latest Apple Watch models, AirPods 5 and updated desktop computers, all of which are also available for pre-order now.


Five major upgrades headline the new iPhone

The iPhone 18 Pro models bring several significant advancements that Apple says represent some of the biggest changes to its flagship phone lineup in years.

  1. A new 48 megapixel Fusion Main camera with variable aperture gives users more creative control over depth of field and lighting than previous models allowed.
  2. New customizable Pro controls in the Camera app make frequently used settings easier to access.
  3. Both models are powered by a new A20 Pro chip paired with a next generation vapor chamber, delivering the highest sustained performance yet in an iPhone.
  4. Updated battery designs offer significantly improved battery life, with the Pro Max model featuring the largest battery life increase in iPhone history.
  5. The phones launch with iOS 27, which introduces a new version of Apple’s Siri assistant built with deeper personal context and expanded artificial intelligence capabilities.

The new iPhones will be available in four finishes, including black, silver, glacier and a new burgundy option.


New Apple Watch and AirPods also launching

Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are also available for pre-order, featuring a new Health Sensing System and chip designed to improve heart rate accuracy. The Series 12 model offers up to 24 hours of battery life, while the Ultra 4 can last up to 50 hours with everyday use.

AirPods 5 round out the new lineup, introducing improved noise cancellation in an open ear design along with a new acoustic architecture aimed at delivering richer sound quality.

All new products, including the iPhone lineup, Apple Watch and AirPods 5, will be available in stores and online starting September 18. Apple’s updated Mac mini and Mac Studio desktop computers will follow, hitting stores September 22.

Ways shoppers can save on new devices

Apple is offering several ways for customers to make the new lineup more affordable at the time of purchase.

Customers trading in an iPhone 13 or newer can receive between $175 and $885 in instant credit. Some carrier partners are offering trade in credit worth up to $1,200 for customers trading in an iPhone 14 or newer toward the new Pro models.

Apple is also offering financing choices, including a leasing program through Klarna with monthly payments starting under $35 for iPhone models, along with zero percent interest installment plans for qualifying United States customers.

New and returning subscribers who purchase the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max can also receive three months of Apple’s subscription bundle Apple One at no cost, granting access to several of the company’s entertainment and cloud storage services.

Apple said in store specialists will be available to help customers select devices, explore financing options and transfer data from older phones during the transition to a new device.

This article was informed by information from Apple Newsroom.

data.title: YouTube TV drops 3 channels, and 1 stays totally free
data.description:
YouTube TV is cutting three channels from its lineup at the end of the month, but before subscribers panic, here is the part the announcement buries. None of these channels is actually disappearing from the internet. Starting Sept. 30, Court TV, Tastemade and The Young Turks will no longer be available on Google’s streaming service, yet all three remain easy to find elsewhere, in most cases completely free. The change is less a loss than a nudge to look somewhere else.


The company notified customers by email, explaining that both live content and anything recorded to a personal library from the three channels will go away once the removal takes effect. The cut also sweeps up two add-on offerings, Tastemade Español, part of the Spanish Plus package, and Tastemade in 4K, part of the 4K Plus tier. YouTube TV noted that members can still watch select content from all three channels on the main YouTube platform.


What each departing channel offers

The three channels serve very different audiences. 1. Tastemade is a food and lifestyle network aimed at home cooks, built around exploring new cuisines and kitchen skills. 2. Court TV, launched in 1991 by lawyer-journalist Steven Brill, made its name with wall-to-wall coverage of major courtroom cases before leaning into prime-time true-crime programming. 3. The Young Turks, which grew out of Cenk Uygur’s public-access show in the 1990s and later became a satellite-radio staple, focuses on current events and political commentary.

Where you can still watch these YouTube TV channels

This is the useful part. Each channel lives on across several other services. Tastemade streams on Prime Video, DIRECTV, Fubo, Philo and Sling TV, plus free platforms including The Roku Channel, Samsung TV Plus and Xumo. Court TV is available on DIRECTV and Fubo, and free on Pluto TV, The Roku Channel and Tubi.


The Young Turks may be the easiest of all to keep up with, since its programming streams free on its own YouTube channel. In other words, a subscriber losing all three on YouTube TV can replace every one of them without paying a cent.

Why this keeps happening

Channel removals like this have become a routine feature of live TV streaming. Services and networks negotiate carriage deals that expire, and when the terms no longer make sense for one side, channels rotate out. For subscribers, the practical takeaway is that the lineup you sign up for is never truly fixed. The upside, at least this time, is that the departing channels are widely available elsewhere, so the disruption comes down to changing where you tune in rather than losing the shows themselves.

data.title: AT&T outage sparks hacking claim, but here’s what really happened
data.description:
AT&T says there is no evidence supporting that claim. The company’s internal assessment points to attempted cable theft as the cause of Monday’s fiber outage, which knocked out internet, TV and phone service for more than 7,000 Dallas area families and caused issues for some Houston customers as well. The claim came from a group calling itself APT IRAN, which posted on Telegram Tuesday saying it had attacked telecommunications and other critical infrastructure across Texas and vowed to keep escalating through Friday, September 11, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks.


How bad was the AT&T outage, and is it over now

Downdetector tracked an initial spike in reports around 2:15 a.m. Monday, followed by a much larger surge near 2:17 p.m. that topped 5,900 reports at its peak. AT&T posted on X that engineering teams were working to restore service, and the outage was largely resolved by 6 p.m. that evening. The company is offering bill credits to customers who experienced at least 20 minutes of qualifying downtime, with details available through its customer service channels.


What actually happens during a copper cable theft

AT&T says copper remains an attractive target for thieves because it can be sold to scrap metal recyclers for cash, even though the metal itself is not scarce. Fiber optic lines, which carry most modern internet traffic, have essentially no resale value since they are made of glass, but thieves sometimes cut them by mistake while trying to reach copper, causing exactly the kind of disruption seen in Dallas.

AT&T’s spokesperson described thieves using tools to cut cable directly off utility poles or climbing into manholes to wrap chains around underground lines and pull them free with vehicles, a practice that has become common enough that AT&T now offers a 10,000 dollar reward for tips leading to an arrest in the Dallas-Fort Worth area.


Is this part of a bigger pattern beyond one outage in Texas

Yes, and this is where the story gets more serious than a single cable cut. APT IRAN has ties to CyberAv3ngers, a hacking persona linked to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps that has been targeting American water utilities, energy systems and now telecommunications networks since a campaign accelerated following February’s U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran.

Federal officials say at least 12 states have reported water system intrusions this year alone, with some incidents causing real operational problems like pressure loss and flooding, even though drinking water itself has remained safe throughout. The FBI, CISA, EPA and NSA have issued multiple joint advisories warning that Iran affiliated actors are exploiting internet exposed industrial control equipment, the same category of infrastructure APT IRAN claims to have hit in Texas.

Why does a law expiring this month matter here

The Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015, which gives utilities and companies legal protection to share threat information with the FBI and CISA without fear of liability, is set to expire September 30 unless Congress renews it.

The law has already lapsed twice in the past year, briefly during last fall’s government shutdown and again in January, and a coalition of more than a dozen trade associations is now pushing Congress to act before the deadline hits again. Critics also point out the law’s current language does not explicitly cover the operational technology, industrial control systems and PLCs that run water treatment plants and similar infrastructure, exactly the equipment this ongoing campaign keeps targeting.

What should people in North Texas actually take from this

For now, AT&T’s own investigation points to a mundane explanation, cable theft rather than a nation state cyberattack, and the company says its network is back to normal. But the claim landing amid a documented, monthslong campaign against American infrastructure means it deserves scrutiny rather than dismissal, especially with a key information sharing law hanging in the balance just weeks away from expiring. Whether this specific outage turns out to be criminal or geopolitical, the broader vulnerability federal agencies keep warning about is not going away on its own.

data.title: iOS 27’s release date is set for Sept. 14: Here’s what new Siri AI can do
data.description:
Apple has officially confirmed that iOS 27 will roll out to compatible iPhones on Monday, September 14, closing months of speculation about when the update would finally leave beta. The headline addition is Siri AI, an Apple Intelligence-powered overhaul that finally gives Siri the kind of conversational depth users have been asking for since Apple first previewed the upgrade back in June.


When and how to download iOS 27

Once the update becomes available on September 14, users will be able to install it by opening the Settings app and navigating to General, then Software Update. Apple recommends backing up a device before installing any major software update in case something needs to be restored afterward.


A few things worth knowing before updating:

  • The most advanced Siri capabilities require an iPhone 15 Pro or newer
  • Older supported iPhones will receive performance and security improvements but will miss out on the newest AI features
  • The update is free for all eligible devices through Software Update
  • Backing up a device beforehand is recommended in case of installation issues

The fold. The aperture. The tiny details.
And iOS 27 landing September 14.

Days like today make me even more excited to keep building Panols. 👀

What caught your eye—Variable aperture, the fold, or something else?#AppleEvent pic.twitter.com/syfe2i1YmV

— Juan Arreguin (@JuanArreguin) September 9, 2026

iOS 27 compatible devices

Not every iPhone will support the update. Here are the devices that work with iOS 27:


  • iPhone SE (second generation or later)

What Siri AI can actually do

Siri now lives in its own dedicated app rather than existing only as a voice prompt layered over the rest of the system. That app gives users a central place to start conversations, review past exchanges, and pick up where a previous request left off, something the assistant has never offered before.

The bigger shift is how Siri understands context. Rather than treating each request as a standalone command, Siri AI can follow a conversation across multiple steps, referencing something mentioned earlier without needing it repeated. It can also pull information from across a phone’s apps and settings to answer more complex, personal questions instead of defaulting to a basic web search.

Other changes coming in iOS 27

Beyond Siri, the update introduces AI-powered photo editing tools, expanded parental controls within Screen Time, and a refined visual language built around Apple’s Liquid Glass design introduced last year. Apple has also added a new iPhone Handoff feature and updated Find My with additional options for hiding a user’s location.

Why the rollout took this long

iOS 27 has been in testing since it was first unveiled at WWDC in June, moving through eight developer betas before reaching public beta testers in July. Apple spent the later stages of testing focused primarily on stability, with recent betas delivering mostly bug fixes and performance refinements, a signal the update was nearing a finished state well before the official date was announced.

What comes next

With the release date now confirmed, attention shifts to how Siri AI performs once it reaches millions of devices outside of controlled beta testing. For users on iPhone 15 Pro or newer, the update represents the fullest, most capable version of Siri Apple has ever shipped. For everyone else running iOS 27 on older hardware, the improvements will be more modest, but the update remains free and available the moment it drops next week.
